query: Generate use cases and test cases for the dashboard feature focusing on chart management, chart limit, and real-time updates.

use_cases.use_case_title: Manage Charts within a Dashboard (Add, Configure, Edit, Delete, Resize, Rearrange) with Chart Limit Enforcement
use_cases.goal: Allow a user to add and manage multiple charts within a dashboard while enforcing the maximum limit of 10 charts.
preconditions: User is authenticated and authorized to edit the selected dashboard (Admin or Editor role as per access control).
At least one dashboard exists and is accessible to the user.
Supported chart types (Bar, Line, Pie, Scatter Plot, Heatmap, Funnel Chart, Gauge Chart, Custom Charts if applicable) are available in the UI.
At least one valid data source is already connected and selectable for charts.
steps: Open dashboard DASH-001 in edit mode.
Add a new chart and select a supported chart type (e.g., Bar Chart).
Configure the chart by selecting a valid data source, defining X-axis and Y-axis values, choosing color schemes and styles, enabling legends, labels, and gridlines, and applying filters and sorting.
Save the chart configuration and verify the chart is added to the dashboard.
Edit the existing chart by changing the data source, chart type, chart labels, and axis settings, then save the changes.
Delete the chart and confirm the deletion when the confirmation prompt appears.
Add charts one by one until the dashboard contains 10 charts.
Attempt to add an 11th chart to the same dashboard.
Resize an existing chart using drag-and-drop to change its size within the dashboard grid.
Rearrange multiple charts using drag-and-drop to change their positions within the dashboard grid.
expected_results: The dashboard opens in edit mode and displays any existing charts (if present).
The system allows selection of any supported chart type when adding a chart.
The chart configuration UI allows selection of data source, X-axis, Y-axis, color schemes, styles, legends, labels, gridlines, filters, and sorting as described.
After saving, the new chart appears on the dashboard and renders data from the selected data source according to the configuration.
Editing the chart updates its data source, type, labels, and axis settings, and the chart re-renders with the new configuration.
When deleting a chart, a confirmation prompt is displayed; upon confirmation, the chart is removed from the dashboard.
The system allows adding charts up to a total of 10 charts on the dashboard without error.
When attempting to add an 11th chart, the system prevents the addition and displays an error message indicating that the chart limit (10) has been reached.
Charts can be resized via drag-and-drop, and the new size is reflected in the dashboard layout.
Charts can be rearranged via drag-and-drop, and their new positions are reflected in the dashboard grid layout.
negative_cases: Attempt to configure a chart with an invalid or disconnected data source (e.g., DISCONNECTED_SOURCE) and verify that the system prevents saving or shows an appropriate error.
Attempt to save a chart without required configuration (e.g., missing X-axis or Y-axis values) and verify that validation errors are shown and the chart is not saved.
Attempt to delete a chart but cancel at the confirmation prompt and verify that the chart remains on the dashboard.
Attempt to add an 11th chart when 10 charts already exist and verify that the system shows an error message and does not add the chart.
Attempt to resize or rearrange charts when the user has only Viewer role and verify that drag-and-drop is not allowed or changes are not persisted.
boundary_cases: Add charts until there are exactly 9 charts, then add the 10th chart and verify it is allowed and no error is shown.
With exactly 10 charts present, attempt to add one more chart and verify that the error message is displayed and the total remains 10.
Resize a chart to the minimum allowed size in the grid and verify that it remains usable and visible.
Resize a chart to the maximum allowed size in the grid (e.g., spanning all columns) and verify that layout remains stable.
Rapidly add and delete charts near the limit (e.g., add to 10, delete 1, add again) and verify that the chart count and limit enforcement remain correct.

use_cases.use_case_title: Configure and Verify Real-time Data Updates for Charts
use_cases.goal: Allow a user to configure auto-refresh intervals for charts and verify that dashboards support real-time data streaming and updates.
preconditions: User is authenticated and has access to view and edit the dashboard.
Dashboard with at least one chart already exists and is connected to a data source that supports real-time data streaming or frequent updates.
The system supports configuration of auto-refresh intervals (1s, 5s, 10s, manual refresh).
steps: Open dashboard DASH-RT-001 that contains chart CH-RT-001 connected to REALTIME_API_WS.
Configure the chart or dashboard settings to set the auto-refresh interval to 1s.
Trigger or simulate a data change in the underlying data source (e.g., new data point or updated values).
Observe the chart for several seconds and verify that it updates in near real-time according to the 1s interval.
Change the auto-refresh interval to 5s and repeat the data change in the data source.
Observe the chart and verify that updates occur approximately every 5 seconds.
Change the auto-refresh interval to 10s and repeat the data change.
Observe the chart and verify that updates occur approximately every 10 seconds.
Set the refresh mode to manual and trigger additional data changes in the data source.
Verify that the chart does not update automatically and only refreshes when the user manually triggers a refresh (e.g., clicking a refresh button).
expected_results: The dashboard and chart load successfully with the current data from REALTIME_API_WS.
The user can select and save an auto-refresh interval of 1s for the chart or dashboard.
When the data source changes, the chart updates in near real-time, reflecting new or changed data according to the 1s interval.
Changing the auto-refresh interval to 5s is saved successfully, and the chart updates approximately every 5 seconds when data changes.
Changing the auto-refresh interval to 10s is saved successfully, and the chart updates approximately every 10 seconds when data changes.
When the refresh mode is set to manual, the chart does not update automatically despite data changes in the source.
When the user manually triggers a refresh in manual mode, the chart fetches and displays the latest data from the data source.
negative_cases: Set an auto-refresh interval and then disconnect the data source; verify that the chart handles the failure gracefully (e.g., shows an error state or no data) without breaking the dashboard.
Attempt to set an unsupported auto-refresh interval value (if the UI allows free input) and verify that the system rejects it or normalizes it to a supported value.
Simulate a scenario where the data source returns invalid or malformed data during a real-time update and verify that the chart does not crash and shows an appropriate error or fallback.
Switch rapidly between different auto-refresh intervals (1s, 5s, 10s, manual) and verify that no duplicate or overlapping refresh requests cause inconsistent chart behavior.
boundary_cases: Run the dashboard with a 1s auto-refresh interval for an extended period and verify that performance remains acceptable and the dashboard continues to update without degradation (within non-functional performance expectations).
Set the auto-refresh interval to the highest available value (10s) and verify that updates still occur reliably at that interval.
Switch from auto-refresh (any interval) to manual mode while an update is in progress and verify that the system transitions cleanly without partial updates.
Open multiple charts on the same dashboard with different auto-refresh intervals and verify that each chart updates independently according to its configured interval.

assumptions: The UI exposes controls to add, configure, edit, delete, resize, and rearrange charts as described in the requirements.
Auto-refresh intervals (1s, 5s, 10s, manual) are configurable either per chart or per dashboard and are visible to the user.
Real-time data streaming is supported by at least one connected data source and is available in the test environment.
Role-based access control is implemented such that Admin and Editor can modify dashboards and charts, while Viewer cannot.
Error messages for exceeding chart limit and data source issues are user-visible, though exact wording is not specified.
missing_info: Exact UI flows and locations of controls for chart management (e.g., where add/edit/delete buttons are placed).
Exact text and format of error messages when the chart limit is exceeded or when data source connections fail.
Whether auto-refresh intervals are configured at the chart level, dashboard level, or both.
Specific behavior when real-time data source is temporarily unavailable (e.g., retry strategy, timeout durations).
Minimum and maximum allowed chart sizes within the grid layout and any snapping rules for resizing.
